CYP450 3A4 and UGT1A1 are the isoenzymes responsible for the metabolic conversion of irinotecan to its inactive metabolite, APC. Inhibition of APC formation results in more irinotecan metabolism to SN-38, an active and toxic metabolite. High plasma levels of irinotecan and SN-38 may increase the risk of potentially fatal toxicities such as severe diarrhea, neutropenia, sepsis, and thromboembolism.
